newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Feb 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Hong Kong Newspaper Headlines-Feb 25.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- China's deceased paramount leader Deng Xiaoping was cremated in Beijing. The ashes will be kept in Zhongnanhai before his family members scatter them into the sea according to his wishes.
-- Commanders of seven major Chinese military regions have pledged allegiance to the leadership of President Jiang Zemin.
-- SING TAO -- To prevent turmoil during the mourning period, China has issued instructions to prohibit overseas pro-democracy activists entering China.
-- WEN WEI PO -- When meeting guests from Portugal, President Jiang Zemin said Macau's handover would draw lessons from Hong Kong's experience.
-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- Facing a competitive property mortgage market, mainland Chinese banks in Hong Kong actively decreased interest rates last year to attract more business.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Several prominent generals and party elders have refused to salute President Jiang Zemin as the "core" of the post-Deng Xiaoping leadership. Sources in Beijing said Jiang's failure to co-opt political foes could spell trouble at this year's 15th Communist Party Congress.
-- The Shenzhen Securities and Exchange Commission and the Shenzhen Stock Exchange are to launch a global roadshow to promote nearly a dozen Shenzhen B-share companies.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- Beijing has issued a nationwide order banning all unofficial gatherings and mourning services for Deng's funeral today.

-- Hong Kong joined five other countries, including the United States and China, in a gathering of central bankers which was seen as an Asian version of the powerful Group of Seven. The "Group of Six" would convene on March 4 in a meeting to be hosted by Japan.

-- Senior officials of China's central bank have reportely urged the financial sector to give full support to the policy of bankruptcy and merger of state enterprises, while stressnng the management of banks' obligatory rights.
